docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

TraefikTLSCertificatesExpiring · critical · for 5m

Meaning

A Traefik-served TLS certificate will expire very soon.

Certificate {{ $labels.cn }} ({{ $labels.sans }}) served by {{ $labels.job }} expires in {{ printf "%.0f" $value }} days, below 7.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

min by (cluster, job, cn, sans) ((last_over_time(traefik_tls_certs_not_after[5m]) - time()) / 86400) < 7

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

TraefikTLSCertificatesExpiringSoon · warning · for 5m

Meaning

A Traefik-served TLS certificate will expire soon.

Certificate {{ $labels.cn }} ({{ $labels.sans }}) served by {{ $labels.job }} expires in {{ printf "%.0f" $value }} days, below 14. Renewal (ACME / cert-manager) should have happened by now.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

min by (cluster, job, cn, sans) ((last_over_time(traefik_tls_certs_not_after[5m]) - time()) / 86400) < 14 > 7

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

TraefikHighHttp5xxErrorRate · warning · for 5m

WireguardPeerHandshakeStale · warning · for 10m

Meaning

WireGuard peer handshake is stale.

WireGuard peer {{ $labels.name }} on {{ $labels.instance }} has not completed a handshake in over 10 minutes.

It fires when the expression below holds for 10m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

wireguard_latest_handshake_seconds > 600

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

GoProcessDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Go process {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(go_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

PhpFpmDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

PHP-FPM pool on {{ $labels.instance }} is unreachable.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

phpfpm_up == 0

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

PumaThreadPoolSaturated · warning · for 10m

Meaning

Puma on {{ $labels.instance }} has kept over 90 percent of its threads busy for 10 minutes.

It fires when the expression below holds for 10m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

100 * puma_busy_threads / clamp_min(puma_max_threads, 1) > 90

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

second by HTTP method. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (method) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Requests by pathing_byPathThe ten busiest host and path combinations. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps topk(10, sum by (host, path) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Requests by statusing_byStatusRequests per second by HTTP status code returned to the client. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (status) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Request bytesing_bytesInRequest bytes received per second (in) and response bytes sent per second (out). nginx_ingress_controller_request_size_sum Bps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_size_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Response bytesing_bytesOutResponse bytes sent to clients per second. nginx_ingress_controller_response_size_sum Bps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_response_size_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — 4xx ratioing_err4xxShare of requests answered with a 4xx (client errors: auth, not found, bad requests). nginx_ingress_controller_requests percentunit sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*", status=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — 5xx ratioing_err5xxShare of requests answered with a 5xx as seen at the ingress (includes upstream failures and nginx 502/503/504). The second line is the 4xx share. nginx_ingress_controller_requests percentunit sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Hostsing_hostsDistinct host names currently serving traffic. nginx_ingress_controller_requests short count(count by (host) (nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"})) — Ingressesing_ingressesDistinct Ingress objects currently serving traffic. nginx_ingress_controller_requests short count(count by (namespace, ingress) (nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"})) — Request p50ing_p50Median request duration at the ingress. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Request p95ing_p9595th percentile of request duration at the ingress. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Request p99ing_p99Request duration as measured by nginx from first byte in to last byte out: p99, p95 and p50. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Requestsing_rateRequests per second arriving through ingress-nginx for the selected Ingress objects. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Upstream errorsing_upstreamErrors502/503/504 answers per second: the backend refused, was unavailable or timed out. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (status) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*", status=~"502\|503\|504"}[$__rate_interval])) — Upstream p99ing_upstreamP99Slowest 1 percent of upstream (backend) response times as seen by nginx. Compare with the request p99: a gap is time spent in nginx or on the client side. nginx_ingress_controller_response_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_response_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"alert-handler.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Pod agekube_ageTime since each pod started. kube_pod_start_time s time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — CPU usagekube_cpuCPU cores used by all containers of each pod (cAdvisor). Dashed lines are the requests and limits from kube-state-metrics: usage above the request means the pod competes for CPU, usage at the limit means it is being throttled. container_cpu_usage_seconds_total short sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])) — CPU limitskube_cpuLimitsCPU limit of the pod containers (above it the kernel throttles). kube_pod_container_resource_limits short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu"}) — CPU requestskube_cpuRequestsCPU requested by the pod containers (what the scheduler reserved). kube_pod_container_resource_requests short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu"}) — Deployment availablekube_deployAvailableDeployment replicas that are available (ready for minReadySeconds). kube_deployment_status_replicas_available short kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"alert-handler.*"} — Deployment desiredkube_deployDesiredReplicas the Deployment spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas actually available. kube_deployment_spec_replicas short kube_deployment_spec_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"alert-handler.*"} — DaemonSet desiredkube_dsDesiredNodes that should run the DaemonSet pod (dashed) versus nodes where it is ready. kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled short kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"alert-handler.*"} — DaemonSet readykube_dsReadyNodes where the DaemonSet pod is ready. kube_daemonset_status_number_ready short kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"alert-handler.*"} — Memory working setkube_memWorking-set memory of each pod (what the kernel would OOM-kill on). Dashed lines are requests and limits: a working set near the limit means an OOM kill is close. container_memory_working_set_bytes bytes sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}) — Memory limitskube_memLimitsMemory limit of the pod containers (the OOM-kill threshold). kube_pod_container_resource_limits bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Memory requestskube_memRequestsMemory requested by the pod containers. kube_pod_container_resource_requests bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Pods not runningkube_notRunningPods in any phase other than Running. kube_pod_status_phase short sum(kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", phase!="Running"} == 1) or vector(0) — Pods by phasekube_phaseNumber of pods in each phase (Running, Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown). kube_pod_status_phase short sum by (phase) (kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Podskube_podsPods matching the selection. kube_pod_info short count(kube_pod_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — PVC usagekube_pvcUsageUsed share of every PersistentVolumeClaim in the namespace, from kubelet volume stats. Not tied to a pod: the whole namespace is shown. kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_byteskubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes percentunit kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} — Containers readykube_readyContainers that pass their readiness probe, per pod. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Containers readykube_readyTotalContainers currently passing their readiness probe. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum(kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Container restartskube_restartsCumulative container restarts per pod. A rising line is a crash loop or a failing liveness probe. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Restarts (1h)kube_restarts1hContainer restarts in the last hour across the selected pods. Anything above zero deserves a look at the Waiting reasons. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) — StatefulSet desiredkube_stsDesiredReplicas the StatefulSet spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_replicas short kube_statefulset_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"alert-handler.*"} — StatefulSet readykube_stsReadyStatefulSet replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready short kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"alert-handler.*"} — Containers waitingkube_waitingContainers stuck in Waiting and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating...). kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason short sum by (pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Containers waitingkube_waitingTotalContainers currently in the Waiting state (not running, not terminated). kube_pod_container_status_waiting short sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Youngest podkube_youngestAge of the most recently started pod. A young pod on a long-running service means a restart or a rollout. kube_pod_start_time dtdurations min(time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Journallogs_journalJournal lines of the systemd unit on the selected hosts, from Loki. — (loki) short {instance=~"$host", unit=~"alert-handler.service"} — Pod logslogs_podLog lines of the selected pods, from Loki. — (loki) short {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — Rule matchesmatchesAlerts matched by each rule per second. alert_handler_rule_matches_total short sum by (rule) (rate(alert_handler_rule_matches_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Process CPUproc_cpuCPU cores used by the process, from its own /metrics (process_cpu_seconds_total). process_cpu_seconds_total short rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]) — FD usageproc_fdRatioOpen file descriptors divided by the process limit. Near 1 new connections and files start failing. process_max_fdsprocess_open_fds percentunit process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} / process_max_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Open file descriptorsproc_fdsFile descriptors the process has open. process_open_fds short process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryproc_rssResident set size reported by the process itself. The dashed line is the virtual address space size. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Uptimeproc_uptimeTime since the process started (process_start_time_seconds). process_start_time_seconds s time() - process_start_time_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Virtual memoryproc_virtVirtual memory size of the process (address space, not RAM used). process_virtual_memory_bytes bytes process_virtual_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryrssResident memory of the handler process. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — RunbooksrunbooksScripts present in the runbook directory. alert_handler_runbooks_available short max(alert_handler_runbooks_available{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — SecretssecretsCredentials read from the secrets directory. alert_handler_secrets_loaded short max(alert_handler_secrets_loaded{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Active unitssystemd_activeUnits in the active state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedUnits in the failed state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedTableUnits currently failed, by host. node_systemd_unit_state short node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1 — Hostssystemd_hostsHosts that have a matching unit at all. node_systemd_unit_state short count(count by (instance) (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"})) — Inactive unitssystemd_inactiveUnits that are loaded but not running. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Unit restartssystemd_restartsService restarts (needs the collector restart metrics: --collector.systemd.enable-restarts-metrics). node_systemd_service_restart_total short sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Unit statesystemd_stateState of each unit on each host: active, transitioning (activating/deactivating), inactive or failed. node_systemd_unit_state short max by (instance, name) ((node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state=~"activating\|deactivating", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"alert-handler.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Taskssystemd_tasksTasks (threads and processes) the unit runs. Needs --collector.systemd.enable-task-metrics. node_systemd_unit_tasks_current short node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task limitsystemd_tasksMaxTasksMax for the unit. Hitting it blocks the unit from forking. node_systemd_unit_tasks_max short node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task usagesystemd_tasksUtilTasks against the unit limit. node_systemd_unit_tasks_currentnode_systemd_unit_tasks_max percent 100 * node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"} / clamp_min(node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"}, 1) — Uptimesystemd_uptimeTime since the unit last started. A drop marks a restart. node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds s time() - node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds{name=~"alert-handler.service", instance=~"$host"} — Webhook errorswebhookErrorsWebhook requests rejected or failed per second (bad payload, auth, internal error). alert_handler_webhook_requests_total short sum(rate(alert_handler_webhook_requests_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|", result!~"ok\|success\|accepted"}[$__rate_interval])) — WebhookswebhooksWebhook requests received per second, by outcome. alert_handler_webhook_requests_total short sum by (result) (rate(alert_handler_webhook_requests_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Process CPUwin_cpuCPU cores used by the matching Windows processes on each host. windows_process_cpu_time_total short sum by (instance) (rate(windows_process_cpu_time_total{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Handleswin_handlesHandles held by the matching Windows processes. Steadily growing means a handle leak. windows_process_handles short sum by (instance) (windows_process_handles{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"}) — Process IOwin_ioBytes read and written by the matching Windows processes per second, by IO mode. windows_process_io_bytes_total Bps sum by (instance, mode) (rate(windows_process_io_bytes_total{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Service statewin_stateState of the Windows service on every host where it exists: running, starting, paused or stopping, stopped (windows_exporter service collector). windows_service_state short max by (instance, name) ((windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)alert-handler", state="running", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)alert-handler", state=~"start pending\|continue pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)alert-handler", state=~"paused\|pause pending\|stop pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)alert-handler", state="stopped", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Threadswin_threadsThreads of the matching Windows processes. windows_process_threads short sum by (instance) (windows_process_threads{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"}) — Process uptimewin_uptimeTime since the oldest matching Windows process started. windows_process_start_time s time() - min by (instance) (windows_process_start_time{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"}) — Working setwin_workingSetWorking set of the matching Windows processes (private bytes where the exporter reports them, otherwise the shared working set). windows_process_working_set_byteswindows_process_working_set_private_bytes bytes sum by (instance) (windows_process_working_set_private_bytes{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"} or windows_process_working_set_bytes{process=~"(?i)alert-handler", instance=~"$host"}) —

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

AlertHandlerDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

alert-handler {{ $labels.instance }} is down; alert actions are not running.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(alert_handler_config_valid[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

docs.title: Alert rules
docs.text: Alert Severity For Expression Runbook AlertmanagerDownAlertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} is down. critical 5m (up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(alertmanager_build_info[1d])) runbook AlertmanagerFailedReloadAlertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} failed to reload its configuration and runs a stale one. critical 10m max_over_time(alertmanager_config_last_reload_successful[5m]) == 0 runbook AlertmanagerClusterFailedPeersAlertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} lost contact with gossip peers; notifications may duplicate or be missed. warning 15m alertmanager_cluster_failed_peers > 0 runbook AlertmanagerFailedToSendAlertsAlertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} fails to send more than 1% of {{ $labels.integration }} notifications. warning 5m sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_failed_total[5m])) / sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_total[5m])) > 0.01 runbook AlertmanagerClusterFailedToSendAlertsEvery Alertmanager instance fails to send more than 1% of {{ $labels.integration }} notifications; the receiver is broken. critical 5m min by (integration) (sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_failed_total[5m])) / sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_total[5m]))) > 0.01 runbook AlertmanagerClusterCrashloopingAlertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} restarted more than 4 times in 10 minutes. critical 0m changes(process_start_time_seconds[10m]) > 4 runbook

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

AlertmanagerDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Alertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(alertmanager_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AlertmanagerFailedReload · critical · for 10m

Meaning

Alertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} failed to reload its configuration and runs a stale one.

It fires when the expression below holds for 10m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

max_over_time(alertmanager_config_last_reload_successful[5m]) == 0

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AlertmanagerClusterFailedPeers · warning · for 15m

Meaning

Alertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} lost contact with gossip peers; notifications may duplicate or be missed.

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

alertmanager_cluster_failed_peers > 0

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AlertmanagerFailedToSendAlerts · warning · for 5m

Meaning

Alertmanager {{ $labels.instance }} fails to send more than 1% of {{ $labels.integration }} notifications.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_failed_total[5m])) / sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_total[5m])) > 0.01

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AlertmanagerClusterFailedToSendAlerts · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Every Alertmanager instance fails to send more than 1% of {{ $labels.integration }} notifications; the receiver is broken.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

min by (integration) (sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_failed_total[5m])) / sum by (instance, integration) (rate(alertmanager_notifications_total[5m]))) > 0.01

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

It fires when the expression below holds for 0m.

docs.text:
Alloy as a service, wherever it runs: its pods, their resources and logs first, then its own metrics, then only the platform tabs that have data (Kubernetes, containers, Docker, systemd, process, ingress, Windows, logs, the Backstage catalog entry), alerts and Kubernetes event annotations.

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

AlloyNoRunningComponents · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Alloy on {{ $labels.instance }} has no running components.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

alloy_component_controller_running_components == 0

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AlloyRemoteWriteFailing · warning · for 15m

Meaning

deployment=~"anomaly-exporter.*"} — Deployment desiredkube_deployDesiredReplicas the Deployment spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas actually available. kube_deployment_spec_replicas short kube_deployment_spec_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"anomaly-exporter.*"} — DaemonSet desiredkube_dsDesiredNodes that should run the DaemonSet pod (dashed) versus nodes where it is ready. kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled short kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"anomaly-exporter.*"} — DaemonSet readykube_dsReadyNodes where the DaemonSet pod is ready. kube_daemonset_status_number_ready short kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"anomaly-exporter.*"} — Memory working setkube_memWorking-set memory of each pod (what the kernel would OOM-kill on). Dashed lines are requests and limits: a working set near the limit means an OOM kill is close. container_memory_working_set_bytes bytes sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}) — Memory limitskube_memLimitsMemory limit of the pod containers (the OOM-kill threshold). kube_pod_container_resource_limits bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Memory requestskube_memRequestsMemory requested by the pod containers. kube_pod_container_resource_requests bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Pods not runningkube_notRunningPods in any phase other than Running. kube_pod_status_phase short sum(kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", phase!="Running"} == 1) or vector(0) — Pods by phasekube_phaseNumber of pods in each phase (Running, Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown). kube_pod_status_phase short sum by (phase) (kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Podskube_podsPods matching the selection. kube_pod_info short count(kube_pod_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — PVC usagekube_pvcUsageUsed share of every PersistentVolumeClaim in the namespace, from kubelet volume stats. Not tied to a pod: the whole namespace is shown. kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_byteskubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes percentunit kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} — Containers readykube_readyContainers that pass their readiness probe, per pod. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Containers readykube_readyTotalContainers currently passing their readiness probe. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum(kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Container restartskube_restartsCumulative container restarts per pod. A rising line is a crash loop or a failing liveness probe. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Restarts (1h)kube_restarts1hContainer restarts in the last hour across the selected pods. Anything above zero deserves a look at the Waiting reasons. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) — StatefulSet desiredkube_stsDesiredReplicas the StatefulSet spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_replicas short kube_statefulset_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"anomaly-exporter.*"} — StatefulSet readykube_stsReadyStatefulSet replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready short kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"anomaly-exporter.*"} — Containers waitingkube_waitingContainers stuck in Waiting and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating...). kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason short sum by (pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Containers waitingkube_waitingTotalContainers currently in the Waiting state (not running, not terminated). kube_pod_container_status_waiting short sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Youngest podkube_youngestAge of the most recently started pod. A young pod on a long-running service means a restart or a rollout. kube_pod_start_time dtdurations min(time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Journallogs_journalJournal lines of the systemd unit on the selected hosts, from Loki. — (loki) short {instance=~"$host", unit=~"anomaly-exporter.service"} — Pod logslogs_podLog lines of the selected pods, from Loki. — (loki) short {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — ModulesmodulesDistinct scoring modules that ran a probe. anomaly_exporter_probes_total short count(count by (module) (anomaly_exporter_probes_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"})) — Probe latencyprobeLatencyHow long the module took. cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Active unitssystemd_activeUnits in the active state. node_systemd_unit_state short (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{name=~"anomaly-exporter.service", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Unit statesystemd_stateState of each unit on each host: active, transitioning docs.title: Alert rules
docs.text: Alert Severity For Expression Runbook AnomalyExporterDownAnomaly exporter {{ $labels.instance }} is down; anomaly scores stop updating. warning 10m (up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(anomaly_exporter_build_info[1d])) runbook AnomalyExporterProbesFailingAnomaly exporter module {{ $labels.module }} fails more than 10% of its probes. warning 15m sum by (module) (rate(anomaly_exporter_probes_total{result!="success"}[10m])) / sum by (module) (rate(anomaly_exporter_probes_total[10m])) > 0.1 runbook AnomalyExporterProbeSlowAnomaly exporter module {{ $labels.module }} probe p99 is above 30s; the module query is too slow for its scrape interval. warning 15m histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, module) (rate(anomaly_exporter_probe_duration_seconds_bucket[10m]))) > 30 runbook

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

AnomalyExporterDown · warning · for 10m

Meaning

Anomaly exporter {{ $labels.instance }} is down; anomaly scores stop updating.

It fires when the expression below holds for 10m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(anomaly_exporter_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AnomalyExporterProbesFailing · warning · for 15m

Meaning

Anomaly exporter module {{ $labels.module }} fails more than 10% of its probes.

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum by (module) (rate(anomaly_exporter_probes_total{result!="success"}[10m])) / sum by (module) (rate(anomaly_exporter_probes_total[10m])) > 0.1

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AnomalyExporterProbeSlow · warning · for 15m

Meaning

Anomaly exporter module {{ $labels.module }} probe p99 is above 30s; the module query is too slow for its scrape interval.

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, module) (rate(anomaly_exporter_probe_duration_seconds_bucket[10m]))) > 30

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

docs.title: Argo CD service
docs.text:
Argo-cd as a service, wherever it runs: its pods, their resources and logs first, then its own metrics, then only the platform tabs that have data (Kubernetes, containers, Docker, systemd, process, ingress, Windows, logs, the Backstage catalog entry), alerts and Kubernetes event annotations.

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

ArgoCdDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Argo CD component {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(argocd_app_info[1d]) or max_over_time(argocd_git_request_total[1d]) or max_over_time(argocd_redis_request_total[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

ArgoCdAppSyncFailed · warning · for 1m

Meaning

Argo CD application {{ $labels.name }} ({{ $labels.project }}) failed to sync in the last 10 minutes.

It fires when the expression below holds for 1m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum by (name, project) (increase(argocd_app_sync_total{phase=~"Error|Failed"}[10m])) > 0

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

PostgresDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

PostgreSQL instance {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

pg_up == 0

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

PostgresHighRollbackRate · warning · for 15m

Meaning

Rollback rate on {{ $labels.instance }} is above 10% of transactions.

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum without (datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback[5m])) / sum without (datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_xact_commit[5m]) + rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback[5m])) > 0.1

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

Meaning

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum without (datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit[5m])) / (sum without (datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit[5m])) + sum without (datname) (rate(pg_stat_database_blks_read[5m]))) < 0.9

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

GoProcessDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Go process {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(go_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

JvmProcessDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

JVM process {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(jvm_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

JvmHighHeapMemory · warning · for 15m

Meaning

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_response_size_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — 4xx ratioing_err4xxShare of requests answered with a (nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*"})) — Request p50ing_p50Median request duration at the ingress. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Request p95ing_p9595th percentile of request duration at the ingress. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Requestsing_rateRequests per second arriving through ingress-nginx for the selected Ingress objects. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Upstream errorsing_upstreamErrors502/503/504 answers per second: the backend refused, was unavailable or timed out. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (status) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*", status=~"502\|503\|504"}[$__rate_interval])) — Upstream p99ing_upstreamP99Slowest 1 percent of upstream (backend) response times as seen by nginx. Compare with the request p99: a gap is time spent in nginx or on the client side. nginx_ingress_controller_response_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_response_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"demo-.*python.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Pod agekube_ageTime since each pod started. kube_pod_start_time s time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — CPU usagekube_cpuCPU cores used by all containers of each pod (cAdvisor). Dashed lines are the requests and limits from kube-state-metrics: usage above the request means the pod competes for CPU, usage at the limit means it is being throttled. container_cpu_usage_seconds_total short sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])) — CPU limitskube_cpuLimitsCPU limit of the pod containers (above it the kernel throttles). kube_pod_container_resource_limits short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu"}) — CPU requestskube_cpuRequestsCPU requested by the pod containers (what the scheduler reserved). kube_pod_container_resource_requests short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu"}) — Deployment availablekube_deployAvailableDeployment replicas that are available (ready for minReadySeconds). kube_deployment_status_replicas_available short kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"demo-.*python.*"} — Deployment desiredkube_deployDesiredReplicas the Deployment spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas actually available. kube_deployment_spec_replicas short kube_deployment_spec_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"demo-.*python.*"} — DaemonSet desiredkube_dsDesiredNodes that should run the DaemonSet pod (dashed) versus nodes where it is ready. kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled short kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"demo-.*python.*"} — DaemonSet readykube_dsReadyNodes where the DaemonSet pod is ready. kube_daemonset_status_number_ready short kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"demo-.*python.*"} — Memory working setkube_memWorking-set memory of each pod (what the kernel would OOM-kill on). Dashed lines are requests and limits: a working set near the limit means an OOM kill is close. container_memory_working_set_bytes bytes sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}) — Memory limitskube_memLimitsMemory limit of the pod containers (the OOM-kill threshold). kube_pod_container_resource_limits bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Memory requestskube_memRequestsMemory requested by the pod containers. kube_pod_container_resource_requests bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Pods not runningkube_notRunningPods in any phase other than Running. kube_pod_status_phase short sum(kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", phase!="Running"} == 1) or vector(0) — Pods by phasekube_phaseNumber of pods in each phase (Running, Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown). kube_pod_status_phase short sum by (phase) (kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Podskube_podsPods matching the selection. kube_pod_info short count(kube_pod_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — PVC usagekube_pvcUsageUsed share of every PersistentVolumeClaim in the namespace, from kubelet volume stats. Not tied to a pod: the whole namespace is shown. kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_byteskubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes percentunit kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} — Containers readykube_readyContainers that pass their readiness probe, per pod. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Containers readykube_readyTotalContainers currently passing their readiness probe. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum(kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Container restartskube_restartsCumulative container restarts per pod. A rising line is a crash loop or a failing liveness probe. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Restarts (1h)kube_restarts1hContainer restarts in the last hour across the selected pods. Anything above zero deserves a look at the Waiting reasons. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) — StatefulSet desiredkube_stsDesiredReplicas the StatefulSet spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_replicas short kube_statefulset_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"demo-.*python.*"} — StatefulSet readykube_stsReadyStatefulSet replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready short kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"demo-.*python.*"} — Containers waitingkube_waitingContainers stuck in Waiting and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating...). kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason short sum by (pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Containers waitingkube_waitingTotalContainers currently in the Waiting state (not running, not terminated). kube_pod_container_status_waiting short sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Youngest podkube_youngestAge of the most recently started pod. A young pod on a long-running service means a restart or a rollout. kube_pod_start_time dtdurations min(time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Journallogs_journalJournal lines of the systemd unit on the selected hosts, from Loki. — (loki) short {instance=~"$host", unit=~"demo-python.service"} — Pod logslogs_podLog lines of the selected pods, from Loki. — (loki) short {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — Max FDsmaxFdsFile-descriptor limit for the process. process_max_fds short process_max_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|", instance=~"$instance"} — Open FDsopenFdsOpen file descriptors. process_open_fds short process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|", instance=~"$instance"} — Process CPUproc_cpuCPU cores used by the process, from its own /metrics (process_cpu_seconds_total). process_cpu_seconds_total short rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]) instance:python_cpu_usage:rate5m FD usageproc_fdRatioOpen file descriptors divided by the process limit. Near 1 new connections and files start failing. process_max_fdsprocess_open_fds percentunit process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} / process_max_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Open file descriptorsproc_fdsFile descriptors the process has open. process_open_fds short process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryproc_rssResident set size reported by the process itself. The dashed line is the virtual address space size. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Uptimeproc_uptimeTime since the process started (process_start_time_seconds). process_start_time_seconds s time() - process_start_time_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Virtual memoryproc_virtVirtual memory size of the process (address space, not RAM used). process_virtual_memory_bytes bytes process_virtual_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryrssResident set size (RSS). process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|", instance=~"$instance"} — Active unitssystemd_activeUnits in the active state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedUnits in the failed state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedTableUnits currently failed, by host. node_systemd_unit_state short node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1 — Hostssystemd_hostsHosts that have a matching unit at all. node_systemd_unit_state short count(count by (instance) (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"})) — Inactive unitssystemd_inactiveUnits that are loaded but not running. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Unit restartssystemd_restartsService restarts (needs the collector restart metrics: --collector.systemd.enable-restarts-metrics). node_systemd_service_restart_total short sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Unit statesystemd_stateState of each unit on each host: active, transitioning (activating/deactivating), inactive or failed. node_systemd_unit_state short max by (instance, name) ((node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state=~"activating\|deactivating", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"demo-python.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Taskssystemd_tasksTasks (threads and processes) the unit runs. Needs --collector.systemd.enable-task-metrics. node_systemd_unit_tasks_current short node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task limitsystemd_tasksMaxTasksMax for the unit. Hitting it blocks the unit from forking. node_systemd_unit_tasks_max short node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task usagesystemd_tasksUtilTasks against the unit limit. node_systemd_unit_tasks_currentnode_systemd_unit_tasks_max percent 100 * node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"} / clamp_min(node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"}, 1) — Uptimesystemd_uptimeTime since the unit last started. A drop marks a restart. node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds s time() - node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds{name=~"demo-python.service", instance=~"$host"} — Process CPUwin_cpuCPU cores used by the matching Windows processes on each host. windows_process_cpu_time_total short sum by (instance) (rate(windows_process_cpu_time_total{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Handleswin_handlesHandles held by the matching Windows processes. Steadily growing means a handle leak. windows_process_handles short sum by (instance) (windows_process_handles{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"}) — Process IOwin_ioBytes read and written by the matching Windows processes per second, by IO mode. windows_process_io_bytes_total Bps sum by (instance, mode) (rate(windows_process_io_bytes_total{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Service statewin_stateState of the Windows service on every host where it exists: running, starting, paused or stopping, stopped (windows_exporter service collector). windows_service_state short max by (instance, name) ((windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)demo-python", state="running", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)demo-python", state=~"start pending\|continue pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)demo-python", state=~"paused\|pause pending\|stop pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)demo-python", state="stopped", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Threadswin_threadsThreads of the matching Windows processes. windows_process_threads short sum by (instance) (windows_process_threads{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"}) — Process uptimewin_uptimeTime since the oldest matching Windows process started. windows_process_start_time s time() - min by (instance) (windows_process_start_time{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"}) — Working setwin_workingSetWorking set of the matching Windows processes (private bytes where the exporter reports them, otherwise the shared working set). windows_process_working_set_byteswindows_process_working_set_private_bytes bytes sum by (instance) (windows_process_working_set_private_bytes{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"} or windows_process_working_set_bytes{process=~"(?i)demo-python", instance=~"$host"}) —

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

PythonProcessDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Python process {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(python_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.
