readykube_dsReadyNodes where the DaemonSet pod is ready. kube_daemonset_status_number_ready short kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"grafana.*"} — Memory working setkube_memWorking-set memory of each pod (what the kernel would OOM-kill on). Dashed lines are requests and limits: a working set near the limit means an OOM kill is close. container_memory_working_set_bytes bytes sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}) — Memory limitskube_memLimitsMemory limit of the pod containers (the OOM-kill threshold). kube_pod_container_resource_limits bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Memory requestskube_memRequestsMemory requested by the pod containers. kube_pod_container_resource_requests bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Pods not runningkube_notRunningPods in any phase other than Running. kube_pod_status_phase short sum(kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", phase!="Running"} == 1) or vector(0) — Pods by phasekube_phaseNumber of pods in each phase (Running, Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown). kube_pod_status_phase short sum by (phase) (kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Podskube_podsPods matching the selection. kube_pod_info short count(kube_pod_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — PVC usagekube_pvcUsageUsed share of every PersistentVolumeClaim in the namespace, from kubelet volume stats. Not tied to a pod: the whole namespace is shown. kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_byteskubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes percentunit kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} — Containers readykube_readyContainers that pass their readiness probe, per pod. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Containers readykube_readyTotalContainers currently passing their readiness probe. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum(kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Container restartskube_restartsCumulative container restarts per pod. A rising line is a crash loop or a failing liveness probe. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Restarts (1h)kube_restarts1hContainer restarts in the last hour across the selected pods. Anything above zero deserves a look at the Waiting reasons. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) — StatefulSet desiredkube_stsDesiredReplicas the StatefulSet spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_replicas short kube_statefulset_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"grafana.*"} — StatefulSet readykube_stsReadyStatefulSet replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready short kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"grafana.*"} — Containers waitingkube_waitingContainers stuck in Waiting and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating...). kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason short sum by (pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Containers waitingkube_waitingTotalContainers currently in the Waiting state (not running, not terminated). kube_pod_container_status_waiting short sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Youngest podkube_youngestAge of the most recently started pod. A young pod on a long-running service means a restart or a rollout. kube_pod_start_time dtdurations min(time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Live channelsliveChannelsActive Grafana Live channels. grafana_live_node_num_channels short sum(grafana_live_node_num_channels{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Live clientsliveClientsClients connected to Grafana Live (websocket streaming). grafana_live_node_num_clients short sum(grafana_live_node_num_clients{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Live messages sentliveSentMessages pushed to Live clients per second. grafana_live_node_messages_sent_count short sum(rate(grafana_live_node_messages_sent_count{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Journallogs_journalJournal lines of the systemd unit on the selected hosts, from Loki. — (loki) short {instance=~"$host", unit=~"grafana(-server)?.service"} — Pod logslogs_podLog lines of the selected pods, from Loki. — (loki) short {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — Notification latency p99notifLatencyP99Slowest 1 percent of notification deliveries to contact points. grafana_alerting_notification_latency_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(grafana_alerting_notification_latency_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Page responsespageStatusHTML page responses per second by status code. grafana_page_response_status_total reqps sum by (code) (rate(grafana_page_response_status_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Plugin request p99pluginP99Slowest 1 percent of backend plugin requests. grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Plugin requestspluginRequestsBackend plugin requests per second, by plugin. grafana_plugin_request_total reqps sum by (plugin_id) (rate(grafana_plugin_request_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Process CPUproc_cpuCPU cores used by the process, from its own /metrics (process_cpu_seconds_total). process_cpu_seconds_total short rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]) — FD usageproc_fdRatioOpen file descriptors divided by the process limit. Near 1 new connections and files start failing. process_max_fdsprocess_open_fds percentunit process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} / process_max_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Open file descriptorsproc_fdsFile descriptors the process has open. process_open_fds short process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryproc_rssResident set size reported by the process itself. The dashed line is the virtual address space size. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Uptimeproc_uptimeTime since the process started (process_start_time_seconds). process_start_time_seconds s time() - process_start_time_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Virtual memoryproc_virtVirtual memory size of the process (address space, not RAM used). process_virtual_memory_bytes bytes process_virtual_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Proxy responsesproxyStatusDatasource proxy responses per second by status code. grafana_proxy_response_status_total reqps sum by (code) (rate(grafana_proxy_response_status_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Rendering queuerenderingQueueImage rendering requests waiting for the renderer. grafana_rendering_queue_size short sum(grafana_rendering_queue_size{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Instance startsrestartsGrafana instance starts in the last hour. Above zero means a crash or a redeploy. grafana_instance_start_total short sum(increase(grafana_instance_start_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[1h])) — Resident memoryrssResident memory of the Grafana process. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Scheduler behindschedulerBehindHow far the alert scheduler is behind its tick. Above a few seconds evaluations are being skipped or delayed. grafana_alerting_scheduler_behind_seconds s max(grafana_alerting_scheduler_behind_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Active unitssystemd_activeUnits in the active state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedUnits in the failed state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedTableUnits currently failed, by host. node_systemd_unit_state short node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1 — Hostssystemd_hostsHosts that have a matching unit at all. node_systemd_unit_state short count(count by (instance) (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"})) — Inactive unitssystemd_inactiveUnits that are loaded but not running. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Unit restartssystemd_restartsService restarts (needs the collector restart metrics: --collector.systemd.enable-restarts-metrics). node_systemd_service_restart_total short sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Unit statesystemd_stateState of each unit on each host: active, transitioning (activating/deactivating), inactive or failed. node_systemd_unit_state short max by (instance, name) ((node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state=~"activating\|deactivating", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Taskssystemd_tasksTasks (threads and processes) the unit runs. Needs --collector.systemd.enable-task-metrics. node_systemd_unit_tasks_current short node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task limitsystemd_tasksMaxTasksMax for the unit. Hitting it blocks the unit from forking. node_systemd_unit_tasks_max short node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task usagesystemd_tasksUtilTasks against the unit limit. node_systemd_unit_tasks_currentnode_systemd_unit_tasks_max percent 100 * node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"} / clamp_min(node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"}, 1) — Uptimesystemd_uptimeTime since the unit last started. A drop marks a restart. node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds s time() - node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds{name=~"grafana(-server)?.service", instance=~"$host"} — Alert rulestotalAlertRulesAlert rules stored. grafana_stat_totals_alert_rules short max(grafana_stat_totals_alert_rules{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — DashboardstotalDashboardsDashboards stored in this instance. grafana_stat_totals_dashboard short max(grafana_stat_totals_dashboard{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — DatasourcestotalDatasourcesDatasources configured. grafana_stat_totals_datasource short max(grafana_stat_totals_datasource{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — FolderstotalFoldersFolders. grafana_stat_totals_folder short max(grafana_stat_totals_folder{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — OrganisationstotalOrgsOrganisations. grafana_stat_total_orgs short max(grafana_stat_total_orgs{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — UserstotalUsersUser accounts. grafana_stat_total_users short max(grafana_stat_total_users{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — UptimeuptimeTime since the Grafana process started. process_start_time_seconds dtdurations min(time() - process_start_time_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Process CPUwin_cpuCPU cores used by the matching Windows processes on each host. windows_process_cpu_time_total short sum by (instance) (rate(windows_process_cpu_time_total{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Handleswin_handlesHandles held by the matching Windows processes. Steadily growing means a handle leak. windows_process_handles short sum by (instance) (windows_process_handles{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"}) — Process IOwin_ioBytes read and written by the matching Windows processes per second, by IO mode. windows_process_io_bytes_total Bps sum by (instance, mode) (rate(windows_process_io_bytes_total{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Service statewin_stateState of the Windows service on every host where it exists: running, starting, paused or stopping, stopped (windows_exporter service collector). windows_service_state short max by (instance, name) ((windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", state="running", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", state=~"start pending\|continue pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", state=~"paused\|pause pending\|stop pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", state="stopped", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Threadswin_threadsThreads of the matching Windows processes. windows_process_threads short sum by (instance) (windows_process_threads{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"}) — Process uptimewin_uptimeTime since the oldest matching Windows process started. windows_process_start_time s time() - min by (instance) (windows_process_start_time{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"}) — Working setwin_workingSetWorking set of the matching Windows processes (private bytes where the exporter reports them, otherwise the shared working set). windows_process_working_set_byteswindows_process_working_set_private_bytes bytes sum by (instance) (windows_process_working_set_private_bytes{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"} or windows_process_working_set_bytes{process=~"(?i)grafana(-server)?", instance=~"$host"}) —

docs.title: Alert rules
docs.text: Alert Severity For Expression Runbook GrafanaDownGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} is down. critical 5m (up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(grafana_build_info[1d])) runbook GrafanaHttpErrorRatioHighGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} is answering more than 5% of requests with a 5xx. warning 15m sum by (instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum by (instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) > 0.05 runbook GrafanaHttpLatencyHighGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} request p99 latency is above 2s. warning 15m histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 2 runbook GrafanaDatabaseConnectionWaitGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} is waiting for database connections — the pool is exhausted. warning 15m rate(grafana_database_conn_wait_count_total[5m]) > 0 runbook GrafanaAlertingSchedulerBehindGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} alert rule scheduler is more than 10s behind. warning 10m grafana_alerting_scheduler_behind_seconds > 10 runbook

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

GrafanaDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Grafana {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(grafana_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

GrafanaHttpErrorRatioHigh · warning · for 15m

Meaning

Grafana {{ $labels.instance }} is answering more than 5% of requests with a 5xx.

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum by (instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum by (instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) > 0.05

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Dashed lines are requests and limits: a working set near the limit means an OOM kill is close. container_memory_working_set_bytes bytes sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}) — Memory limitskube_memLimitsMemory limit of the pod containers (the OOM-kill threshold). kube_pod_container_resource_limits bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Memory requestskube_memRequestsMemory requested by the pod containers. kube_pod_container_resource_requests bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Pods not runningkube_notRunningPods in any phase other than Running. kube_pod_status_phase short sum(kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", phase!="Running"} == 1) or vector(0) — Pods by phasekube_phaseNumber of pods in each phase (Running, Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown). kube_pod_status_phase short sum by (phase) (kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Podskube_podsPods matching the selection. kube_pod_info short count(kube_pod_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — PVC usagekube_pvcUsageUsed share of every PersistentVolumeClaim in the namespace, from kubelet volume stats. Not tied to a pod: the whole namespace is shown. kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_byteskubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes percentunit kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} — Containers readykube_readyContainers that pass their readiness probe, per pod. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Containers readykube_readyTotalContainers currently passing their readiness probe. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum(kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Container restartskube_restartsCumulative container restarts per pod. A rising line is a crash loop or a failing liveness probe. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Restarts (1h)kube_restarts1hContainer restarts in the last hour across the selected pods. Anything above zero deserves a look at the Waiting reasons. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) — StatefulSet desiredkube_stsDesiredReplicas the StatefulSet spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_replicas short kube_statefulset_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"grafana.*"} — StatefulSet readykube_stsReadyStatefulSet replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready short kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"grafana.*"} — Containers waitingkube_waitingContainers stuck in Waiting and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating...). kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason short sum by (pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Containers waitingkube_waitingTotalContainers currently in the Waiting state (not running, not terminated). kube_pod_container_status_waiting short sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Youngest podkube_youngestAge of the most recently started pod. A young pod on a long-running service means a restart or a rollout. kube_pod_start_time dtdurations min(time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Live channelsliveChannelsActive Grafana Live channels. grafana_live_node_num_channels short sum(grafana_live_node_num_channels{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Live clientsliveClientsClients connected to Grafana Live (websocket streaming). grafana_live_node_num_clients short sum(grafana_live_node_num_clients{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Live messages sentliveSentMessages pushed to Live clients per second. grafana_live_node_messages_sent_count short sum(rate(grafana_live_node_messages_sent_count{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Journallogs_journalJournal lines of the systemd unit on the selected hosts, from Loki. — (loki) short {instance=~"$host", unit=~"grafana-test.service"} — Pod logslogs_podLog lines of the selected pods, from Loki. — (loki) short {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — Notification latency p99notifLatencyP99Slowest 1 percent of notification deliveries to contact points. grafana_alerting_notification_latency_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(grafana_alerting_notification_latency_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Page responsespageStatusHTML page responses per second by status code. grafana_page_response_status_total reqps sum by (code) (rate(grafana_page_response_status_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Plugin request p99pluginP99Slowest 1 percent of backend plugin requests. grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(grafana_plugin_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Plugin requestspluginRequestsBackend plugin requests per second, by plugin. grafana_plugin_request_total reqps sum by (plugin_id) (rate(grafana_plugin_request_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Process CPUproc_cpuCPU cores used by the process, from its own /metrics (process_cpu_seconds_total). process_cpu_seconds_total short rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]) — FD usageproc_fdRatioOpen file descriptors divided by the process limit. Near 1 new connections and files start failing. process_max_fdsprocess_open_fds percentunit process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} / process_max_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Open file descriptorsproc_fdsFile descriptors the process has open. process_open_fds short process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryproc_rssResident set size reported by the process itself. The dashed line is the virtual address space size. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Uptimeproc_uptimeTime since the process started (process_start_time_seconds). process_start_time_seconds s time() - process_start_time_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Virtual memoryproc_virtVirtual memory size of the process (address space, not RAM used). process_virtual_memory_bytes bytes process_virtual_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Proxy responsesproxyStatusDatasource proxy responses per second by status code. grafana_proxy_response_status_total reqps sum by (code) (rate(grafana_proxy_response_status_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) — Rendering queuerenderingQueueImage rendering requests waiting for the renderer. grafana_rendering_queue_size short sum(grafana_rendering_queue_size{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Instance startsrestartsGrafana instance starts in the last hour. Above zero means a crash or a redeploy. grafana_instance_start_total short sum(increase(grafana_instance_start_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[1h])) — Resident memoryrssResident memory of the Grafana process. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Scheduler behindschedulerBehindHow far the alert scheduler is behind its tick. Above a few seconds evaluations are being skipped or delayed. grafana_alerting_scheduler_behind_seconds s max(grafana_alerting_scheduler_behind_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Active unitssystemd_activeUnits in the active state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedUnits in the failed state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedTableUnits currently failed, by host. node_systemd_unit_state short node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1 — Hostssystemd_hostsHosts that have a matching unit at all. node_systemd_unit_state short count(count by (instance) (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", instance=~"$host"})) — Inactive unitssystemd_inactiveUnits that are loaded but not running. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Unit restartssystemd_restartsService restarts (needs the collector restart metrics: --collector.systemd.enable-restarts-metrics). node_systemd_service_restart_total short sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{name=~"grafana-test.service", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Unit statesystemd_stateState of each unit on each host: active, transitioning (activating/deactivating), inactive or failed. node_systemd_unit_state short max by (instance, name) ((node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state=~"activating\|deactivating", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"grafana-test.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Taskssystemd_tasksTasks (threads and processes) the unit runs. Hitting it blocks the unit from forking. node_systemd_unit_tasks_max short node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"grafana-test.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task usagesystemd_tasksUtilTasks against the unit limit. node_systemd_unit_tasks_currentnode_systemd_unit_tasks_max percent 100 * node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"grafana-test.service", instance=~"$host"} / clamp_min(node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"grafana-test.service", instance=~"$host"}, 1) — Uptimesystemd_uptimeTime since the unit last started. docs.title: Alert rules
docs.text: Alert Severity For Expression Runbook GrafanaDownGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} is down. critical 5m (up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(grafana_build_info[1d])) runbook GrafanaHttpErrorRatioHighGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} is answering more than 5% of requests with a 5xx. warning 15m sum by (instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count{status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum by (instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) > 0.05 runbook GrafanaHttpLatencyHighGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} request p99 latency is above 2s. warning 15m histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, instance) (rate(grafana_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 2 runbook GrafanaDatabaseConnectionWaitGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} is waiting for database connections — the pool is exhausted. warning 15m rate(grafana_database_conn_wait_count_total[5m]) > 0 runbook GrafanaAlertingSchedulerBehindGrafana {{ $labels.instance }} alert rule scheduler is more than 10s behind. warning 10m grafana_alerting_scheduler_behind_seconds > 10 runbook

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

GrafanaDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Grafana {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(grafana_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

docs.title: k8s-monitoring (Alloy) service
docs.text:
K8s-monitoring as a service, wherever it runs: its pods, their resources and logs first, then its own metrics, then only the platform tabs that have data (Kubernetes, containers, Docker, systemd, process, ingress, Windows, logs, the Backstage catalog entry), alerts and Kubernetes event annotations.

Library g.libs.services.k8sMonitoring Board observ-viz-svc-k8s-monitoring in Platform / Monitoring / Collectors · not rendered Wraps Alloy (g.libs.collector.alloy): its signals, alerts and rules are part of this board's Collectors app-exporters / apps, cadvisor / container, kube-state-metrics / kube, kubelet / kubelet, node_exporter / systemd, windows_exporter / other, windows_exporter / service Contents 89 signals · 65 metrics · 4 alert rules with runbooks · 2 recording rules · the board

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

AlloyNoRunningComponents · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Alloy on {{ $labels.instance }} has no running components.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

alloy_component_controller_running_components == 0

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

AlloyRemoteWriteFailing · warning · for 15m

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

LokiDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Loki {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(loki_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

Many non-voluntary switches mean CPU contention. namedprocess_namegroup_context_switches_total ops sum by (instance, groupname, ctxswitchtype) (rate(namedprocess_namegroup_context_switches_total{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Worst FD ratiohproc_fdRatioOpen descriptors of the worst process divided by its soft limit. Near 1 the process starts failing with too many open files. namedprocess_namegroup_worst_fd_ratio percentunit max by (instance, groupname) (namedprocess_namegroup_worst_fd_ratio{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Open file descriptorshproc_fdsOpen file descriptors across the process group. namedprocess_namegroup_open_filedesc short sum by (instance, groupname) (namedprocess_namegroup_open_filedesc{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Process readhproc_ioReadBytes read from storage by the process group per second, with writes alongside. namedprocess_namegroup_read_bytes_total Bps sum by (instance, groupname) (rate(namedprocess_namegroup_read_bytes_total{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Process writehproc_ioWriteBytes written to storage by the process group per second. namedprocess_namegroup_write_bytes_total Bps sum by (instance, groupname) (rate(namedprocess_namegroup_write_bytes_total{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Major page faultshproc_majFaultsMajor page faults per second: the process is reading pages back from disk, a sign of memory pressure. namedprocess_namegroup_major_page_faults_total short sum by (instance, groupname) (rate(namedprocess_namegroup_major_page_faults_total{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Processeshproc_procsProcesses in the group. More than expected usually means forks or workers piling up. namedprocess_namegroup_num_procs short sum by (instance, groupname) (namedprocess_namegroup_num_procs{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Process RSShproc_rssResident memory of the process group. namedprocess_namegroup_memory_bytes bytes sum by (instance, groupname) (namedprocess_namegroup_memory_bytes{groupname=~"mimir", memtype="resident", instance=~"$host"}) — Process stateshproc_statesProcesses of the group by kernel state (Running, Sleeping, Waiting, Zombie, Other). namedprocess_namegroup_states short sum by (instance, groupname, state) (namedprocess_namegroup_states{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Threadshproc_threadsThreads across the process group. namedprocess_namegroup_num_threads short sum by (instance, groupname) (namedprocess_namegroup_num_threads{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Process uptimehproc_uptimeTime since the oldest process of the group started. namedprocess_namegroup_oldest_start_time_seconds dtdurations time() - min by (instance, groupname) (namedprocess_namegroup_oldest_start_time_seconds{groupname=~"mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Requests by hosting_byHostRequests per second by Ingress host name. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (host) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Requests by ingressing_byIngressRequests per second by Ingress object. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (namespace, ingress) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Requests by methoding_byMethodRequests per second by HTTP method. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (method) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Requests by pathing_byPathThe ten busiest host and path combinations. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps topk(10, sum by (host, path) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Requests by statusing_byStatusRequests per second by HTTP status code returned to the client. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (status) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Request bytesing_bytesInRequest bytes received per second (in) and response bytes sent per second (out). nginx_ingress_controller_request_size_sum Bps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_size_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Response bytesing_bytesOutResponse bytes sent to clients per second. nginx_ingress_controller_response_size_sum Bps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_response_size_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — 4xx ratioing_err4xxShare of requests answered with a 4xx (client errors: auth, not found, bad requests). nginx_ingress_controller_requests percentunit sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*", status=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — 5xx ratioing_err5xxShare of requests answered with a 5xx as seen at the ingress (includes upstream failures and nginx 502/503/504). The second line is the 4xx share. nginx_ingress_controller_requests percentunit sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Hostsing_hostsDistinct host names currently serving traffic. nginx_ingress_controller_requests short count(count by (host) (nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"})) — Ingressesing_ingressesDistinct Ingress objects currently serving traffic. nginx_ingress_controller_requests short count(count by (namespace, ingress) (nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"})) — Request p50ing_p50Median request duration at the ingress. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Request p95ing_p9595th percentile of request duration at the ingress. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Request p99ing_p99Request duration as measured by nginx from first byte in to last byte out: p99, p95 and p50. nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Requestsing_rateRequests per second arriving through ingress-nginx for the selected Ingress objects. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum(rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval])) — Upstream errorsing_upstreamErrors502/503/504 answers per second: the backend refused, was unavailable or timed out. nginx_ingress_controller_requests reqps sum by (status) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*", status=~"502\|503\|504"}[$__rate_interval])) — Upstream p99ing_upstreamP99Slowest 1 percent of upstream (backend) response times as seen by nginx. Compare with the request p99: a gap is time spent in nginx or on the client side. nginx_ingress_controller_response_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_response_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", service=~"mimir.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Ingester seriesingesterSeriesSeries held in ingester memory. Drives ingester memory and the head block size. cortex_ingester_memory_series short sum(cortex_ingester_memory_series{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}) — Pod agekube_ageTime since each pod started. kube_pod_start_time s time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — CPU usagekube_cpuCPU cores used by all containers of each pod (cAdvisor). Dashed lines are the requests and limits from kube-state-metrics: usage above the request means the pod competes for CPU, usage at the limit means it is being throttled. container_cpu_usage_seconds_total short sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])) — CPU limitskube_cpuLimitsCPU limit of the pod containers (above it the kernel throttles). kube_pod_container_resource_limits short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu"}) — CPU requestskube_cpuRequestsCPU requested by the pod containers (what the scheduler reserved). kube_pod_container_resource_requests short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu"}) — Deployment availablekube_deployAvailableDeployment replicas that are available (ready for minReadySeconds). kube_deployment_status_replicas_available short kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"mimir.*"} — Deployment desiredkube_deployDesiredReplicas the Deployment spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas actually available. kube_deployment_spec_replicas short kube_deployment_spec_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"mimir.*"} — DaemonSet desiredkube_dsDesiredNodes that should run the DaemonSet pod (dashed) versus nodes where it is ready. kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled short kube_daemonset_status_desired_number_scheduled{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"mimir.*"} — DaemonSet readykube_dsReadyNodes where the DaemonSet pod is ready. kube_daemonset_status_number_ready short kube_daemonset_status_number_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", daemonset=~"mimir.*"} — Memory working setkube_memWorking-set memory of each pod (what the kernel would OOM-kill on). Dashed lines are requests and limits: a working set near the limit means an OOM kill is close. container_memory_working_set_bytes bytes sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!=""}) — Memory limitskube_memLimitsMemory limit of the pod containers (the OOM-kill threshold). kube_pod_container_resource_limits bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Memory requestskube_memRequestsMemory requested by the pod containers. kube_pod_container_resource_requests bytes sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory"}) — Pods not runningkube_notRunningPods in any phase other than Running. kube_pod_status_phase short sum(kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", phase!="Running"} == 1) or vector(0) — Pods by phasekube_phaseNumber of pods in each phase (Running, Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Unknown). kube_pod_status_phase short sum by (phase) (kube_pod_status_phase{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Podskube_podsPods matching the selection. kube_pod_info short count(kube_pod_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — PVC usagekube_pvcUsageUsed share of every PersistentVolumeClaim in the namespace, from kubelet volume stats. Not tied to a pod: the whole namespace is shown. kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_byteskubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes percentunit kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace"} — Containers readykube_readyContainers that pass their readiness probe, per pod. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Containers readykube_readyTotalContainers currently passing their readiness probe. kube_pod_container_status_ready short sum(kube_pod_container_status_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Container restartskube_restartsCumulative container restarts per pod. A rising line is a crash loop or a failing liveness probe. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Restarts (1h)kube_restarts1hContainer restarts in the last hour across the selected pods. Anything above zero deserves a look at the Waiting reasons. kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total short sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) — StatefulSet desiredkube_stsDesiredReplicas the StatefulSet spec asks for (dashed) versus replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_replicas short kube_statefulset_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"mimir.*"} — StatefulSet readykube_stsReadyStatefulSet replicas that are ready. kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready short kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", statefulset=~"mimir.*"} — Containers waitingkube_waitingContainers stuck in Waiting and why (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ContainerCreating...). kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason short sum by (pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} == 1) — Containers waitingkube_waitingTotalContainers currently in the Waiting state (not running, not terminated). kube_pod_container_status_waiting short sum(kube_pod_container_status_waiting{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Youngest podkube_youngestAge of the most recently started pod. A young pod on a long-running service means a restart or a rollout. kube_pod_start_time dtdurations min(time() - kube_pod_start_time{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) — Journallogs_journalJournal lines of the systemd unit on the selected hosts, from Loki. — (loki) short {instance=~"$host", unit=~"mimir.service"} — Pod logslogs_podLog lines of the selected pods, from Loki. — (loki) short {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} — Process CPUproc_cpuCPU cores used by the process, from its own /metrics (process_cpu_seconds_total). process_cpu_seconds_total short rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]) — FD usageproc_fdRatioOpen file descriptors divided by the process limit. Near 1 new connections and files start failing. process_max_fdsprocess_open_fds percentunit process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} / process_max_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Open file descriptorsproc_fdsFile descriptors the process has open. process_open_fds short process_open_fds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Resident memoryproc_rssResident set size reported by the process itself. The dashed line is the virtual address space size. process_resident_memory_bytes bytes process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Uptimeproc_uptimeTime since the process started (process_start_time_seconds). process_start_time_seconds s time() - process_start_time_seconds{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — Virtual memoryproc_virtVirtual memory size of the process (address space, not RAM used). process_virtual_memory_bytes bytes process_virtual_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"} — QueriesqueriesQueries handled by the query frontend per second. cortex_query_frontend_queries_total reqps sum(rate(cortex_query_frontend_queries_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) instance:cortex_queries:rate5m Received samplesreceivedSamplesSamples the distributor accepts per second, the ingest volume. cortex_distributor_received_samples_total short sum(rate(cortex_distributor_received_samples_total{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval])) instance:cortex_received_samples:rate5m Request p99requestP99Slowest 1 percent of requests across all Mimir components. cortex_request_duration_seconds_bucket s histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le)(rate(cortex_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace\|", pod=~"$pod\|"}[$__rate_interval]))) — Active unitssystemd_activeUnits in the active state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedUnits in the failed state. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Failed unitssystemd_failedTableUnits currently failed, by host. node_systemd_unit_state short node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1 — Hostssystemd_hostsHosts that have a matching unit at all. node_systemd_unit_state short count(count by (instance) (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"})) — Inactive unitssystemd_inactiveUnits that are loaded but not running. node_systemd_unit_state short count(node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) or vector(0) — Unit restartssystemd_restartsService restarts (needs the collector restart metrics: --collector.systemd.enable-restarts-metrics). node_systemd_service_restart_total short sum by (instance, name) (increase(node_systemd_service_restart_total{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Unit statesystemd_stateState of each unit on each host: active, transitioning (activating/deactivating), inactive or failed. node_systemd_unit_state short max by (instance, name) ((node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="active", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state=~"activating\|deactivating", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="inactive", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (node_systemd_unit_state{name=~"mimir.service", state="failed", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Taskssystemd_tasksTasks (threads and processes) the unit runs. Needs --collector.systemd.enable-task-metrics. node_systemd_unit_tasks_current short node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task limitsystemd_tasksMaxTasksMax for the unit. Hitting it blocks the unit from forking. node_systemd_unit_tasks_max short node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"} — Task usagesystemd_tasksUtilTasks against the unit limit. node_systemd_unit_tasks_currentnode_systemd_unit_tasks_max percent 100 * node_systemd_unit_tasks_current{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"} / clamp_min(node_systemd_unit_tasks_max{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"}, 1) — Uptimesystemd_uptimeTime since the unit last started. A drop marks a restart. node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds s time() - node_systemd_unit_start_time_seconds{name=~"mimir.service", instance=~"$host"} — Process CPUwin_cpuCPU cores used by the matching Windows processes on each host. windows_process_cpu_time_total short sum by (instance) (rate(windows_process_cpu_time_total{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Handleswin_handlesHandles held by the matching Windows processes. Steadily growing means a handle leak. windows_process_handles short sum by (instance) (windows_process_handles{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Process IOwin_ioBytes read and written by the matching Windows processes per second, by IO mode. windows_process_io_bytes_total Bps sum by (instance, mode) (rate(windows_process_io_bytes_total{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) — Service statewin_stateState of the Windows service on every host where it exists: running, starting, paused or stopping, stopped (windows_exporter service collector). windows_service_state short max by (instance, name) ((windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)mimir", state="running", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 1 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)mimir", state=~"start pending\|continue pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 2 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)mimir", state=~"paused\|pause pending\|stop pending", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 3 or (windows_service_state{name=~"(?i)mimir", state="stopped", instance=~"$host"} == 1) * 4) — Threadswin_threadsThreads of the matching Windows processes. windows_process_threads short sum by (instance) (windows_process_threads{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Process uptimewin_uptimeTime since the oldest matching Windows process started. windows_process_start_time s time() - min by (instance) (windows_process_start_time{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"}) — Working setwin_workingSetWorking set of the matching Windows processes (private bytes where the exporter reports them, otherwise the shared working set). windows_process_working_set_byteswindows_process_working_set_private_bytes bytes sum by (instance) (windows_process_working_set_private_bytes{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"} or windows_process_working_set_bytes{process=~"(?i)mimir", instance=~"$host"}) —

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

MimirDown · critical · for 5m

Meaning

Mimir {{ $labels.instance }} is down.

It fires when the expression below holds for 5m.

Impact

Something users depend on is already broken or about to be. Treat it as an incident.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(cortex_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

MimirHighRequestLatency · warning · for 15m

Meaning

Request p99 latency on {{ $labels.instance }} is above 1s.

It fires when the expression below holds for 15m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(cortex_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 1

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
One per alert rule - the runbook the rule carries, or one generated from it - the text the board's Runbooks tab shows. A rule without a written runbook links to its page here, runbooks/<alert>/, which shows the same text.

OpencostDown · warning · for 10m

Meaning

OpenCost {{ $labels.instance }} is down; cost data stops.

It fires when the expression below holds for 10m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

(up == 0) and on (job, instance) (max_over_time(opencost_build_info[1d]))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

OpencostNoNodeCostData · warning · for 30m

Meaning

OpenCost is exporting no node cost data.

It fires when the expression below holds for 30m.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

absent(node_total_hourly_cost)

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

OpencostClusterCostJump · warning · for 1h

Meaning

Cluster node cost is more than 50% above yesterday: nodes were added or repriced.

It fires when the expression below holds for 1h.

Impact

Nothing is broken yet, and it will be if the trend holds. Look at it this working day.

Diagnosis

Run the alert expression and look at which series cross the threshold:

sum(node_total_hourly_cost) > 1.5 * sum(avg_over_time(node_total_hourly_cost[1d] offset 1d))

Then open this board with the same selectors: the tab that carries those metrics shows how long the series has been where it is, and the restart and deploy annotations show whether a release or a restart lines up with the change.

Mitigation

  • Confirm the target is the one you think it is: check the labels on the firing series.
  • Compare against the same series on a healthy peer; a single instance out of line is a different problem from every instance moving together.
  • If a deploy or restart lines up with the change, that is the first thing to undo.
  • If the threshold no longer matches how this service behaves, change the rule rather than living with a permanent alert.

Prometheus as a service, wherever it runs: its pods, their resources and logs first, then its own metrics, then only the platform tabs that have data (Kubernetes, containers, Docker, systemd, process, ingress, Windows, logs, the Backstage catalog entry), alerts and Kubernetes event annotations.
